'''Jonathan Rodney Brockman''' (born March 20, 1987) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He was the starting [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] and team captain for the [[University of Washington]] [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|men's basketball team]]. He is the University of Washington's all-time leading rebounder and second-all-time leading scorer in University of Washington history. He grabbed the 1,000th rebound of his career on December 30, 2008, in a win over [[Morgan State Bears men's basketball|Morgan State]],<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20090205074830/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=283650264 Morgan State 67, Washington 81 - Recap - December 30, 2008]</ref> and became Washington's all-time leading rebounder on January 15, 2009, in a win over [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]], breaking [[Doug Smart]]'s school record of 1,051.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20090131060514/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290152483 Washington 84, Oregon 67 - Recap - January 15, 2009]</ref>

==High school career==
Brockman attended [[Snohomish High School]] and was a 4-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]]. He played alongside his brother for two years. He averaged 22 points per game and 13 rebounds per game as a junior.

In his senior year, he led Snohomish to a 16–5 record, averaging 29.8 points per game and 12 rebounds per game. He was ranked as the 20th-best prospect in the country and 5th-best among power forwards by Scout.com.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&cfg=bb&pid=44&yr=2005|title=Scout.com College Basketball Team Recruiting Prospects|work=[[Scout.com]]|access-date=February 11, 2013}}</ref> He was named to the [[McDonald's All-American Game]]<ref name="highschool-stats">{{cite web|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/022405aaa.html|title=Brockman and Webster named to 2005 McDonald's All-American Team|work=GoHuskies.com|date=February 24, 2005|access-date=February 11, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110711104536/http://www.gohuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/022405aaa.html|archive-date=July 11, 2011}}</ref> and made the semifinals in the 2005 High School Slam Dunk Competition. He was the third-leading scorer in the [[Washington (state)|state of Washington]] in the 2004–05 season, and was one of the best rebounders in the class of 2005.<ref name="highschool-stats" />

Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Brockman was listed as the No. 13 power forward and the No. 47 player in the nation in 2005.<ref>[https://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Jon-Brockman-22049;_ylt=Atfr4.CWZ_kCV7ARPBLHv.zXO5B4 Jon Brockman Recruiting Profile]</ref>

==College career==
He played alongside future [[NBA]] players [[Brandon Roy]] and [[Bobby Jones (basketball, born 1984)|Bobby Jones]] and was named to the [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-10]] all-freshman team. He played in the [[2006 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2006 NCAA tournament]], in which [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]] lost to [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|UConn]] in the Sweet 16. Brockman led the Huskies in rebounds and was 7th in the Pac-10. He ended the season with four double-doubles. He has the second-highest total rebounds by a freshman in Husky history and was ranked 2nd in the Pac-10 with his 51.8 field goal percentage.

==Professional career==

=== Sacramento Kings (2009–2010) ===
Brockman was selected 38th overall in the [[2009 NBA draft]] by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], and his rights were later traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] for the rights to [[Jeff Ayres|Jeff Pendergraph]]. He averaged 5.4 points and 9.2 rebounds in the [[NBA Summer League|Las Vegas Summer League]] following the draft.

=== Milwaukee Bucks (2010–2012) ===
On July 21, 2010, Brockman was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] for [[Darnell Jackson]] and a [[2011 NBA draft|2011 second-round draft pick]] in a [[sign-and-trade]], signing a 3-year, $3 million contract.<ref>{{cite web | title = Bucks Acquire Brockman from Kings | url = http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/brockman_release_100721.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = 2010-07-21 | access-date = 2010-07-21 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20100724081633/http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/brockman_release_100721.html | archive-date = 2010-07-24 | url-status = dead }}</ref>

=== Limoges CSP (2012–2013) ===
On June 27, 2012, Brockman, [[Jon Leuer]], [[Shaun Livingston]], and a draft pick were traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] for [[Samuel Dalembert]] and draft picks.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-receive-12th-overall-pick-trade-bucks Rockets Receive 12th Overall Pick Via Trade With Bucks]. NBA.com. June 27, 2012. Retrieved on June 27, 2012.</ref> On October 29, Brockman was waived by Houston.<ref>{{cite web | title = Houston Rockets Cut Livingston, Hayward, Forbes, Brockman And Johnson | url = http://spacecityscoop.com/2012/10/29/houston-rockets-cut-livingston-hayward-forbes-brockman-and-johnson/ | work = [[SI.com]] | date = 2012-10-29 | access-date = 2012-10-29 | archive-date = November 3, 2014 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141103191254/http://spacecityscoop.com/2012/10/29/houston-rockets-cut-livingston-hayward-forbes-brockman-and-johnson/ | url-status = dead }}</ref> On November 18, 2012, he signed with [[Limoges CSP]] of France for the rest of the 2012–13 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Limoges tabs Jon Brockman|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/96642/limoges-tabs-jon-brockman.html|access-date=November 3, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=November 18, 2012}}</ref>

=== Élan Chalon (2013–2014) ===
In 2013, Brockman played for the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in the [[NBA Summer League|Las Vegas Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Pelicans giving Jon Brockman a shot at Summer League | url = http://www.rotoinfo.com/playerupdate/194366/Jon-Brockman-F/ | work = rotoinfo.com | date = 2012-07-03 | access-date = 2012-07-14 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://archive.today/20130717075655/http://www.rotoinfo.com/playerupdate/194366/Jon-Brockman-F/ | archive-date = 2013-07-17 }}</ref> On June 6, 2013, he signed with [[Élan Chalon]] of France for the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=ELAN CHALON adds Slaughter, Brockman |url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2013-14/i/114277/8174/elan-chalon-adds-slaughter-brockman |access-date=November 3, 2014 |work=Eurocupbasketball.com |date=June 6, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130628042433/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2013-14/i/114277/8174/elan-chalon-adds-slaughter-brockman |archive-date=June 28, 2013 }}</ref>

=== Riesen Ludwigsburg (2014–2016) ===
On November 1, 2014, Brockman was signed by the German club [[MHP Riesen Ludwigsburg]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/139668/mhp-riesen-ludwigsburg-lands-jon-brockman.html MHP Riesen Ludwigsburg lands Jon Brockman]</ref>

After playing overseas for four seasons, Brockman decided to retire prior to the beginning of the 2016–17 season.

== Coaching career ==
Brockman worked as a head coach for the [[Granite Falls, Washington|Granite Falls]] Middle School 7th-grade boys' basketball team.<ref>[http://www.heraldnet.com/sports/ex-nba-player-brockman-enjoying-coach-role/ Ex-NBA player returns home to coach at Snohomish High]</ref> He now works as an agricultural education teacher for his alma mater, Snohomish High School, while also helping to coach the boys' basketball team on which he once starred.
